name: Northwest Registered Agent
subcategory: legal documents, privacy compliance and business administration
tagline: Track entity deadlines and documents without serving as a legal registered agent

tiers.name: Registered Agent
tiers.limits: $125/year per state; service in all 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico; online document scans and compliance reminders

tiers.name: LLC / Corporation Formation
tiers.limits: $39 one-time service fee plus state fees; first year of registered-agent service included

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; first-year registered-agent service is bundled only with the paid $39 formation order plus state fees
pricing.billingTerms: registered agent billed annually; formation is one-time
pricing.hiddenCosts: Government/state formation fees are mandatory and vary by state. Registered-agent service renews at $125/year after the included first year.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Northwest Registered Agent, track entity deadlines and documents without serving as a legal registered agent. The hard boundary is physical agent network, mail handling, state compliance, privacy, and support, plus expert judgment, compliance, and regulated services.
coreLoopDIY: Track entity deadlines and documents, fill clearly labeled templates, track versions and approvals, and repeatedly state that outputs require qualified review, without serving as a legal registered agent.
requirements: jurisdiction-specific templates supplied by the user or counsel
whatYouLose: physical agent network, mail handling, state compliance, privacy, and support
moatNotes: expert judgment, compliance, and regulated services
ongoingBurden: law changes, jurisdiction, template provenance, access, signatures, filings, deadlines, evidence, retention, security, and professional liability
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Northwest Registered Agent because the durable value is expert accountability and regulated execution; document generation alone cannot supply either. The recurring cost buys law changes, jurisdiction, template provenance, access, signatures, filings, deadlines, evidence, retention, security, and professional liability, not just the visible interface.

prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Northwest Registered Agent in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a versioned Markdown template engine; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track entity deadlines and documents, fill clearly labeled templates, track versions and approvals, and repeatedly state that outputs require qualified review, without serving as a legal registered agent.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create versioned questionnaires, reusable fact fields, conditional sections, templates, and approval states.
Show the source, jurisdiction, owner, reviewed date, and expiry date for every template.
Generate DOCX and PDF drafts with prominent draft and review-required labels.
Keep an immutable audit log of answers, template version, generation time, downloads, and approvals.
Add role-based access, retention, export, encrypted backups, and a deadline calendar.
Display legal-review warnings before generation and again before any final download.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out legal advice or guaranteed compliance.
Deliberately leave out government filings, identity verification, and registered-agent services.
Deliberately leave out automatic consent decisions or deployment without qualified review.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
